title: fix(lint): capability-reference-unknown reads providers over the artifact being built
body:
Fixes #32575
domain:spec#2 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcSbLCxEmyHf9upz3pz · branch `claude/issue-32575-capability-provider-artifact-scope`

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:`capability-reference-unknown` 这条作者期 lint 在逐包检查时,也把同一个制品(artifact)里其它包声明的能力和授权算作"已提供"。
- **为什么改**:A 包的应用要求某能力、B 包的权限集授予它时,构建会误报"这道门永远关闭";运行时其实放行。误报会诱导作者删掉有效的门或重复授权。
- **风险与回滚**:风险低,只影响一条警告级规则,不改契约、不改运行时;回滚即 revert 本 PR。整个制品里都没人提供的能力照旧告警。
- **先看**:`packages/lint/src/validate-capability-references.ts`(第 110–126 行,`addProvidersOf` 与 `packagesOf` 循环);其测试文件新增的 describe 块;`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` 的两段解释文字。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/validate-capability-references.test.ts`,预期 21 条全绿。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`os build`, `os validate` and `os lint` run the author-time rule table twice on a multi-package artifact: once over the union, once per package (`runPerPackageAuthoringRules`, `packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts:307`). The per-package pass hands each rule one package body plus the artifact's `packages[]` as resolution context (`packageBodyAsStack`, `:186`). By the ruled design recorded there, the consuming rule decides which contents of that context it reads. `validateCapabilityReferences` read none of it. It took capability providers (`stack.capabilities`, `stack.permissions[].systemPermissions`) from the judged package only. So a gate in package A that a permission set in package B grants got the false "fails closed" warning. The union run saw the grant, so its de-duplication key never matched and the per-package finding survived.

The runtime does not scope a capability to a package. `resolveAuthzContext` folds the `systemPermissions` of every set the caller holds into one list, whichever package declared the set (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:2077`, assigned at `:880`; the sets come from the security catalog, `:1699`). Every `requiredPermissions` gate asks only whether that list names the capability: `missingCapabilities` (`packages/runtime/src/required-capabilities.ts:33`) for actions and flows, and `filterAppForUserWithReason` over `ctx.systemPermissions` for apps (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:1735`). That scope is the whole installed environment, which is wider than the artifact. So the artifact is the widest scope the author-time lint can see, and reading it never makes the lint more lenient than the runtime.

The fix is on the rule side, where the scope is decided, following the triage direction ("read providers over the artifact being built, as the runtime does. No contract change."):

- `packages/lint/src/validate-capability-references.ts` now reads `capabilities` and `permissions[].systemPermissions` from every `packages[].manifest` too, through the shared `packagesOf` reader (`object-graph.ts`, the same reader `validate-object-references.ts` uses for sibling objects). The references it judges are still only the given stack's own. The verdict and the fix line do not change. The flows judgement (ruling record 6377848497, letter A) is untouched; only the provider scope moved.
- `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`: the `os explain capability-reference-unknown` text now says that a sibling package's grant counts and why, and that the lint reads every package of the artifact being built but cannot see other installed packages.
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`: one sentence said "a single package's lint cannot see capabilities declared by *other* installed packages". This change made it false, so it now says the same scope as the explanation.
- No change to the CLI caller: it already passes the artifact's `packages[]` as resolution context. The scope was the rule's decision, so the fix is in the rule.

## Tests

`packages/lint/src/validate-capability-references.test.ts` gains a describe block. It builds the exact stack shape `packageBodyAsStack` produces (`{ ...body, manifest: body, packages }`):

- package A requires `crm_marketing_app` and sibling B grants it through `systemPermissions` → no finding;
- sibling B declares it with `defineCapability` → no finding;
- a capability no package of the artifact provides still warns (`rule`, `severity: 'warning'`, `where`, `path` asserted), and the granted reference next to it stays clean;
- siblings are resolution context only: a typo in B's own app is not reported when A is judged (lit control: judging B reports it).

The explanation pins gain `every package of the artifact being built`. The test that checks each source silences the rule gains the two sibling-package sources.

<details><summary>Reproduction through the real per-package pass (scratch probe, not committed)</summary>

A two-package artifact: A = `com.acme.marketing` (app `crm_marketing` requires `crm_marketing_app`; app `crm_typo` requires `crm_markting_app`), B = `com.acme.app` (permission set granting `crm_marketing_app`). The probe calls `runAuthoringRules('build', …)` (union) and `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` from `packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts`, against the built `@objectstack/lint`.

Before (origin/main `8bfbc4ed`):

```text
UNION [ "app \"crm_typo\" :: requiredPermissions names capability \"crm_markting_app\", which no built-in, `defineCapability` or `systemPermissions` grant provides, so this gate fails closed" ]
PER-PACKAGE [ "package 'com.acme.marketing' — app \"crm_marketing\" :: requiredPermissions names capability \"crm_marketing_app\", which no built-in, `defineCapability` or `systemPermissions` grant provides, so this gate fails closed" ]
```

After (`b718045c`, lint rebuilt):

```text
UNION [ "app \"crm_typo\" :: requiredPermissions names capability \"crm_markting_app\", ... so this gate fails closed" ]
PER-PACKAGE []
```

The genuine typo is still reported. The false per-package warning is gone.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (one-shot, committed fix first)</summary>

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `addProvidersOf(body as AnyRec);` with `void body; /* ABLATED */` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `e794c731203f` → `31ce2ebe3c2d`). The test imports the rule from `src` by relative path, so no build leg was needed. Result: `Tests 5 failed | 16 passed (21)`. That is the four new cases plus the source-silencing case. The "still warns" case went red too, because under the ablation the granted reference warns as well (2 findings, 1 expected). Restore: blob after restore == HEAD (`e794c731203f`), `git diff HEAD` empty.

</details>

<details><summary>Package tests and typecheck (head b718045c)</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` → `Test Files 199 passed (199)`, `Tests 8513 passed (8513)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` (tsc + `check:test-typecheck`) → `VERDICT command-exit 0`, "check:test-typecheck: OK".
- The public surface is byte-unchanged (same export and signature), so no importer owes a test.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Scope reached: an artifact's packages. A capability provided only by a package installed from a different artifact still warns. That is the existing, documented reason the rule is a warning, and the runtime's wider scope (the whole environment) means this direction can only over-warn, never under-warn.
- `packagesOf` refuses a present non-array `packages` (`INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES`, 422), as every other rule reading sibling packages does (ruling A on the `packages` shape). A parsed stack never carries one. The Studio preview caller (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/preview/capabilityLint.ts`) passes no `packages` key.
- The message text did not change. The issue's alternative ("name the package scope in the message") is not needed once the scope matches the runtime.

## Verification

<details><summary>Local gate set — `dispatch-gates --commands` derived on this diff (96 families), head b718045c</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran` (exit codes recorded) → `96 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 92 run, 4 NOT-MEASURED (4 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`.

92 families exit 0. NOT MEASURED, each an exit-3 prerequisite refusal (CI runs them on a full checkout and build):

- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`: the positive control is pinned to commit `621a4876`, which this shallow clone cannot reach;
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples`: no spec declarations built in this worktree;
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: reads every package's `dist/`; only the lint closure is built;
- `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure`: needs `packages/objectql/dist`.

`node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` → exit 0. The control-byte self-scan over the five changed files found nothing.

</details>
